title: Digital SAT: Format & the Adaptive Modules
summary: The ~2h14m Digital SAT — two sections, two adaptive modules each, scored 400–1600 — and what the module design means for you.

nodes.label: On Bluebook app
nodes.note: Digital, with a built-in Desmos calculator & timer

chunks.heading: Two sections, two modules each
chunks.body: The Digital SAT has two sections — **Reading and Writing (RW)** and **Math** — and each is split into **two separately-timed modules**. RW is **54 questions in 64 minutes** (two 32-minute modules of 27); Math is **44 questions in 70 minutes** (two 35-minute modules of 22). Total testing time is about **2 hours 14 minutes**.
chunks.realExample: You do RW module 1, then module 2, then Math module 1, then module 2. Within a module you can move freely — flag a hard question and come back before the module's timer ends.
chunks.memoryHook: 2 sections × 2 modules. RW = 54 in 64; Math = 44 in 70. ~2h14m total.

chunks.heading: It's multistage adaptive
chunks.body: Each section is **two-stage adaptive**: **module 1 has a broad mix of easy, medium and hard questions**, and **how you do on module 1 sets whether module 2 is harder or easier** — which in turn sets your score ceiling. So module 1 is the high-leverage part.
chunks.realExample: Do well on RW module 1 and module 2 serves a harder set worth more points; a weaker module 1 routes you to an easier module 2 with a lower ceiling. Treat module 1 as the one that matters most.
chunks.memoryHook: Module 1 decides module 2 — and your ceiling. No coasting on the first module.

chunks.heading: Scored 400–1600
chunks.body: You get a **section score of 200–800 for Reading and Writing and 200–800 for Math**, added to a **total of 400–1600**. There's **no penalty for wrong answers**, so never leave a question blank.
chunks.realExample: A 1400 might be RW 700 + Math 700, or RW 650 + Math 750 — colleges see both the total and the sections, so a balanced profile and a strong total both help.
chunks.memoryHook: 200–800 per section → 400–1600 total. No wrong-answer penalty — always answer.

chunks.heading: Digital, with built-in tools
chunks.body: The test runs in the **Bluebook app** with an **on-screen timer, a mark-for-review flag, annotation, and a built-in Desmos graphing calculator you can use on all of Math**. Practise in Bluebook first so the tools are second nature on test day.
chunks.realExample: The Desmos calculator can graph equations to solve them visually — learning it before test day turns some Math questions into a quick graph-and-read.
chunks.memoryHook: Bluebook + Desmos (all of Math) + flag tool. Rehearse the app before test day.

recall.q: What are the two sections of the Digital SAT and how long is each?
recall.a: Reading and Writing (54 questions, 64 minutes) and Math (44 questions, 70 minutes) — about 2 hours 14 minutes total.

recall.q: How is each SAT section structured?
recall.a: Into two separately-timed modules; the second module's difficulty depends on your performance on the first (two-stage adaptive).
Your performance on module 1 determines whether module 2 is harder or easier — and therefore your scoring ceiling.

recall.q: What is the SAT score range and is there a wrong-answer penalty?
recall.a: 400–1600 (200–800 per section), with no penalty for wrong answers — so never leave a blank.

recall.q: What tools are available in the Bluebook app?
recall.a: An on-screen timer, a mark-for-review flag, annotation, and a built-in Desmos graphing calculator usable on all Math questions.
